source.author: cic
source.text: Namque illos veteres doctores auctoresque dicendi nullum genus disputationis a se alienum putasse accepimus semperque esse in omni orationis ratione versatos; ex quibus Elius Hippias, cum Olympiam venisset maxima illa quinquennali celebritate ludorum, gloriatus est cuncta paene audiente Graecia nihil esse ulla in arte rerum omnium quod ipse nesciret; nec solum has artis, quibus liberales doctrinae atque ingenuae continerentur, geometriam, musicam, litterarum cognitionem et poetarum atque illa, quae de naturis rerum, quae de hominum moribus, quae de rebus publicis dicerentur, se tenere sed anulum, quem haberet, pallium, quo amictus, soccos, quibus indutus esset, se sua manu confecisse.
source.text_original: Namque illos veteres doctores auctoresque dicendi nullum genus disputationis a se alienum putasse accepimus semperque esse in omni orationis ratione versatos; / ex quibus Elius Hippias, cum Olympiam venisset maxima illa quinquennali celebritate ludorum, gloriatus est cuncta paene audiente Graecia nihil esse ulla in arte rerum omnium quod ipse nesciret; nec solum has artis, quibus liberales doctrinae atque ingenuae continerentur, geometriam, musicam, litterarum cognitionem et poetarum atque illa, quae de naturis rerum, quae de hominum moribus, quae de rebus publicis dicerentur, se tenere sed anulum, quem haberet, pallium, quo amictus, soccos, quibus indutus esset, se sua manu confecisse.
source.text_english: For we have learned that those ancient teachers and founders of eloquence thought no kind of discussion foreign to them, and were always engaged in every branch of speaking; among them, when Euthias Hippias had come to Olympia at that great quinquennial celebration of the games, he boasted before almost all Greece as his hearers that there was nothing in any art concerning all subjects that he himself did not know; and that he was master not only of those arts embraced by liberal and free education—geometry, music, the study of letters, and the works of poets—and of those matters treated concerning the nature of things, human character, and public affairs, but also that the ring he wore, the cloak with which he was clothed, and the shoes he had on, he had made with his own hand.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: unde et apud Graecos philosophus ille laudatur, qui omne, quod uteretur, usque ad pallium et anulum manu sua factum gloriatus est.
reuse.text_original: unde et apud Graecos philosophus ille laudatur, qui omne, quod uteretur, usque ad pallium et anulum manu sua factum gloriatus est.
reuse.text_english: Hence among the Greeks too that philosopher is praised, who boasted that everything he used, even to his cloak and ring, had been made by his own hand.
